source_title: Open-source image editor focused on PSD compatibility and workflows familiar to Adobe Photoshop users. - GitHub
source_excerpt:
A free, open-source image editor for Windows, macOS, Linux, and the browser, made with game art and pixel art in mind. It focuses on accurate PSD compatibility, keeping text, vectors, masks, layer styles, and Smart Objects editable in layered Photoshop files, and its workflows and keyboard shortcuts will feel familiar if you know Photoshop. Paint in limited palettes without flattening your layers, bring in Affinity, Krita, GIMP, OpenRaster, Paint.NET, and PDF artwork, and extend the editor with classic plug-ins and JavaScript.
Download · Try in your browser · Features · Full gallery
For bug reports and feature requests, please open an issue or post in Discussions . These are the best places to post because search engines can index them, helping others find the questions and answers. Want to chat? Join Seth's Discord .
Latest release: 1.30 · November 9, 2026 · Release notes · All releases
Windows releases are code signed by Seth A. Robinson; the macOS app is signed and notarized (Robinson Technologies Corporation); the Linux Flatpak repository is GPG signed. Every release is published on the GitHub Releases page with SHA-256 checksums.
Paste this into a terminal to install the Flatpak for your user (no root needed). It pulls the shared KDE runtime from Flathub, and the same command installs the ARM64 build on a Raspberry Pi 5 or another 64-bit ARM computer.
Patchy then updates with flatpak update and starts from your application menu. The Linux install guide covers getting the flatpak tool, system-wide installs, the single-file bundle, Raspberry Pi setup, and the AppImage (FUSE, menu entries, updates).
Click an image for the full-size capture.
See the full gallery for seamless tiling with the Dink Smallwood palette, layer styles, vector tools, Warp Text and type, artboards, scanning (Divide Scanned Photos, Scan a Book to PDF), the G'MIC and GEGL filter libraries, Tilt-Shift and other filters, palette mode, Camera Raw, Perspective Planes, and more.
Full feature list and format support · Installing Photoshop plug-ins · Scripting guide · AI control setup
No telemetry or tracking. Your images leave your computer only if you use the optional OpenAI Image Tools with your own API key.
Optional update checks contact GitHub. One-click updates (Windows and the Linux AppImage) and Object Selection's High Quality model are downloaded only when you ask for them.
The browser build runs the same editor locally through WebAssembly. Desktop builds have more memory available and add printing, scanner and camera import, and command-line automation.
Twelve interface languages, dark and light schemes, and importable themes are included.
The desktop and browser builds share the editor, with these differences:
Format support does not imply every source feature stays editable; see the format limits and current limitations . PDF import requires Qt PDF when building a custom desktop version. HEIC/HEIF availability depends on the installed decoder . The browser build also has tighter memory limits.
In the October 29, 2026 Testy v2 run , Patchy opened all 309 files of the psd-tools test collection, and Photoshop reopened every Patchy save with all 43 text objects, 183 adjustment layers, 172 Smart Objects, and 181 live effects kept. Patchy's perceptual render match was 98.7% , with 299 files within 10% of Photoshop's pixels, and its Photoshop text score was 97.3% , both the highest of the six programs tested against Photoshop's reference, using a Patchy 1.21 development build (commit 25822a64 ).
Testy v2 scores each program on what it draws itself: the baked pixels Photoshop stores for text, shapes, fills, and Smart Objects are removed first. That is stricter than the August run, so the two sets of numbers are not comparable.
These are dated, corpus-specific results. The linked report has every file's renders and difference maps for all seven columns. Read the full comparison and methodology for the tables, per-folder results, scoring rules, and limitations.
Know the limits: editing is RGB at 8, 16, or 32 bits per channel (the browser build stops at 16). CMYK work is proofing and export: CMYK Proof mode shows the print colors and saves CMYK JPEG, TIFF, and PDF, but pixels stay RGB. Lab and the other color modes convert to RGB on open, and there is no GPU acceleration. Unsupported Smart Filters can remain preview-locked, and Affinity import has format-specific limitations. See current compatibility .
Scan a Book to PDF (experimental): File > Import > Scan a Book to PDF scans a bound book one spread per key press, finds each page, and writes a PDF whose pages all share one size, covers included. It keeps the book in a project folder you can continue later, sets pages per scan while scanning, lets you adjust the labeled spine lines, and exports in color, grayscale or black and white. So far it has only been tested by hand on Windows, so treat it as experimental, especially on macOS and Linux
Brushes: Smudge has its own Strength setting (default 50%) instead of using the brush Opacity ( issue 675 ); big Airbrush, Flow and soft brush strokes keep up with the cursor ( issue 677 ), and so do 700 px and larger Dodge, Burn, Sponge and Smudge strokes ( issue 660 ); a 1 px brush with Flow under 100 paints a continuous line; Blur, Smudge, Sharpen and the healing tools handle edges against transparency, and Blur softens a layer's edge; Alt+Shift shows the Shift+click line preview on Dodge, Burn, Blur and Sharpen ( issue 662 )
Text: the Type options bar has Bold, Italic, Underline, a Justify toggle and a right-to-left toggle, and anti-aliasing moves to the Character panel ( issue 673 ); Paragraph adds Justify Last Centered, Justify Last Right and Justify All, read and saved in PSDs ( issue 672 ); the new Type Mask tool turns typed letters into a selection ( issue 670 ); a missing font shows its family and its style in separate fields, and the PSD compatibility report no longer lists preserved image resources or embedded smart object sources ( issue 669 )
Layers panel: the filter menu finds layers by type, properties, row color or Selected Only, combined with the name text ( issue 671 )
Shapes: dragging a whole shape with Path Select keeps up ( issue 678 ); polygons reopened from a PSD stay live, and the Shape picker shows the shape that was stamped ( issue 643 , issue 644 , issue 622 )
Hotkeys: Preferences > Hotkeys has a Show list for all, menu, tool, other or assigned commands ( issue 676 ); the GIMP-style and Krita-style sets put tool modifiers on Ctrl as their manuals do ( issue 302 ), and in the GIMP-style set N, K and A pick the Pencil, Ink and Airbrush brush presets ( issue 645 )
Also: on Windows 11 the window keeps its minimize and maximize animations and gets a theme-colored border, and a narrow menu bar folds into an overflow menu before reaching the window buttons ( issue 674 ); Customize Tool Palette can hide the scroll-wheel expand button and the scroll arrows ( issue 668 ); filter dialogs put Preview beside Reset and remember it ( issue 667 ); Export for Web encodes GIF and PNG previews of 3 megapixels or more once their row is selected, with a faster color quantizer ( issue 571 ); the save prompt offers No to All when several unsaved documents close; commands that need a layer say so instead of doing nothing
See build instructions for the core, Qt desktop app, macOS, Linux, and Windows packaging. Contributors and automation tools should read AGENTS.md first.
Patchy is released under the MIT License on every platform. Third-party runtime notices are tracked in NOTICE-THIRD-PARTY.md .
Some packages also carry separately licensed libraries: every desktop package includes GEGL (GNU LGPL, with its GPL-3 operations module), and the Linux Flatpak includes SANE (GNU GPL) and libgphoto2 (GNU LGPL) for scanner and camera import. Their license texts ship inside the package, and each release publishes their source next to the downloads as PatchyGeglSources.zip and PatchyLinuxScannerSources.zip . These licenses cover those libraries; Patchy's own code stays MIT.

This project was developed with significant assistance from AI tools. I mean, you can still blame me (Seth) for bugs, but I just wanted to mention it.
Note: All included textures/materials are real images taken by humans, not AI generated.
AI has reached the point where you can use your favorite AI agent to add the missing feature you want.
Just give it the link to this repo and tell it "read AGENTS.md and add feature X to this project". It will read the code, read the tests, and add the feature.
I mean, that's kind of the power of open source, amplified.
Whatever AI you use (the smarter the better), tell it (or more likely, it's reading this right now) to read AGENTS.md before doing anything else. It contains the build and repository-wide rules, then routes feature work to the relevant document under docs/ .
There are thousands of regression and benchmarking tests. AGENTS.md links agents to the testing guide that explains how to select and run them. Due to the size of some of the test files I use they aren't all included, it will skip tests that require missing files.
I probably don't want any major features coming from outside, as there are wrong and right ways to do things, some of it a bit subjective. Remember, you can always go crazy in your own fork, have some fun!
If you have a bug fix or feature you think fits this project's scope please open an issue or tweet/etc at me. If you want to submit a pull request, please look at the actual code and fully TEST IT YOURSELF before submitting, and if possible include screenshots of the actual changes so it's clear what you're doing. If you're using AI, use a good one (Fable/Astra+ class), we don't want barely working slop.
Don't trust AI to create and submit PRs with no oversight, I'll delete ones that have too much AI smell. Smell human. This is starting to sound weird but you know what I mean.
Independent development and compatibility
Patchy is an independently developed image editor. Our goal is to build something powerful, fast, free of unnecessary bloat, and ultimately a tool that fits what I'm doing, especially for game-dev use cases. Recreating Photoshop feature for feature is not the goal.
Our PSD compatibility work uses publicly available format documentation and observations of files and rendered output produced by a licensed copy of Photoshop. We have not decompiled or disassembled Photoshop. Patchy also implements the legacy 8BF plug-in interface for interoperability, using its own declarations without copying Adobe SDK code. This compatibility work helps people keep their documents editable and use existing plug-ins across applications.
We also take patents seriously. Some features are deliberately limited or omitted because of patent concerns. For example, Quick Select calculates the selection when you finish a stroke instead of updating it continuously as you paint. Our development constraints document these boundaries, which we revisit as relevant patents expire or our research changes.
